subject: Streamly SLO options, tradeoffs, and next asks
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Thompson <ben.thompson@streamly.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — Streamly performance constraints and tradeoffs

Ben — thanks for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a shared starting point and clear asks: 

Key SLOs and traffic profile (from today's deck):
- Target: p95 latency <= 120ms for single-turn streaming responses (server-sent events)
- Typical steady-state throughput: ~120 req/s with 15% peak bursts (~140 req/s)
- Target concurrency: 300 concurrent user sessions with active streaming connections
- Avg tokens per response: 40-90 tokens; 95th percentile ~160 tokens for longer responses

Primary constraints and priorities you stated:
- Priority 1: consistent low p95 (user-facing latency)
- Priority 2: predictable unit cost; budget target ~ $X per 1M requests (we'll capture exact numbers from your procurement)
- Priority 3: observability/traceability (per-request traces + token-level cost)

Cost/perf levers we should evaluate (initial suggestions):
- Continuous batching (short micro-batch windows) vs. strict real-time (trade latency smoothing for cost)
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (we'll need sample logs to estimate hit rates)
- Quantization profiles (FP16 vs. 4-bit mixed; expected latency savings vs. quality risk)
- Model variants / routing (small variant for short queries, large for long/high-quality streams)

Attached: streamly-metrics-sample.csv (traffic shapes you referenced) and a quick mutual-action-plan.xlsx that maps responsibilities.

Next asks from Redwood:
1) Can you share a 7-day sample of production traffic (timestamps + tokens/request + typical prompt length) — we can estimate batching/caching impact from that.
2) Confirm the hard p95 SLA window (is 120ms hard or a phased goal?).
3) Procurement timeline + any stamping authority for cost decisions (cc Aisha if procurement owns this).

I'll loop Marcus & Irene on the infra/engineering tradeoffs and propose an initial PoC configuration that hits p95 target while showing cost delta.

Thanks,
Karthik
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Streamly performance constraints and tradeoffs

Karthik — appreciate the clear recap. Couple clarifications from our side: 

- 120ms p95 is the aspirational target for interactive exploration UI; for batch-like exports we can tolerate higher latency but that isn't streaming. So yes — treat 120ms as the priority for the streaming path.
- We'll upload a 7-day traffic sample (anonymized) by EOD tomorrow — that'll include tokens/request and peak-minute slices. Attaching our internal projection (prod-traffic-projection.csv).
- Procurement: Aisha (cc) will own cost approvals; our target for decision is end of Q2. We may request a 3-month PoC credit while legal reviews terms.

Also, two extra items:
1) Security/compliance: we need a short note on data retention and whether tokens are logged in plaintext (we prefer limited token-level logs; can you outline options).
2) Streaming behavior expectation: we sometimes stream partial generation early; how does Redwood's batching/caching interact with early-token streaming? Will batching delay first-byte?

Thanks — Ben
Head of Integrations, Streamly

Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Streamly performance constraints and tradeoffs

Ben / team — quick technical notes from infra/serving perspective (summarizing tradeoffs we should run in PoC):

1) Continuous batching and first-byte latency:
- We can run sub-10ms batching windows that group tokens across inflight requests; in practice this typically adds ~5-12ms median depending on concurrency. For your p95 target we should test with 5ms, 10ms, and 20ms windows to quantify tail.
- For early-token streaming (stream partial generation), Redwood supports progressive flush — batching only aggregates when it doesn't block first-byte (configurable). We'll preserve first-byte streaming at the cost of lower batch efficiency.

2) Caching assumptions:
- Prefix/KV cache works well for repeated prompts or shared system messages. Hit-rate depends on prompt entropy — with your sample logs we can estimate hit rate. 30% hit gives large token cost savings without impacting latency for hits.

3) Quantization and model variants:
- Recommend evaluating a 4-bit quantized medium variant for short responses and a high-quality fp16 large for long-form. We expect ~20-35% CPU/GPU microsecond reduction on 4-bit for transformer matmuls; quality delta typically small on short replies but may appear on long-form edge cases.

4) Observability & telemetry:
- To debug p95 we need per-request trace (routing, batching delta, cache hit/miss, quantization path). We'll ship a small instrumentation SDK you can drop into your proxy to report these fields (PII-safe).

Action items for PoC (my suggestions):
- Redwood provides two config arms: (A) Low-latency primary: 5ms batch window + prefix caching + dynamic routing to medium-quantized model for <=90 token responses; (B) Cost-optimized: 15ms batch window + more aggressive quantization and routing. We'll measure p50/p95 and cost per 1k tokens.
- Provide 7-day logs + current model prompts. Redwood to run an offline simulation to estimate hit rates and expected token savings.

Happy to run a short technical deep-dive this week if useful.

—Marcus
Senior Systems Engineer, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

Subject: Redwood next steps & proposed PoC plan (timeline + deliverables)

Ben / Aisha — thanks for the prompt reply and for agreeing to share the traffic sample. Below is a concise plan so procurement and engineering know timelines and deliverables.

PoC objectives (2-4 weeks):
- Demonstrate p95 <= 120ms on streaming path for a representative 1-week workload slice
- Measure unit cost delta across two config arms and document quality-impact notes for quantized paths
- Deliver instrumentation dashboard (per-route latency, cache-hit, batching window, token cost)

Proposed timeline:
- Day 0-3: Streamly uploads anonymized 7-day sample + procurement provides target budget constraints and procurement timeline
- Day 3-7: Redwood runs offline simulation and returns expected p95/cost range and recommended PoC config (A vs B)
- Week 2: Short PoC (2-4 days) in Redwood sandbox region using Streamly sample traffic; shared dashboard & logs
- Week 3-4: Optional canary run in your staging with live traffic if PoC metrics look good

Required from Streamly:
- 7-day traffic sample (anonymized) — tokens/request + prompt hashes preferable
- Confirmation that 120ms p95 is the streaming hard target
- Procurement contact and decision window (Aisha please confirm)

I attached a short Redwoods SLO playbook (redwood-slo-playbook-v1.pdf) and the mutual-action-plan.xlsx to this thread. We'll also share a Drive link with the proposed PoC config and the instrumentation spec.

If that plan looks good I'll coordinate a kickoff and get Marcus assigned to run the sim and PoC. Proposed kickoff: Thu Apr 1 10:00am PT — does that work for you?

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
